title: Opset matcher autotuner for variable-latency inference workloads
creator: Sofia Chen
description: Goal: build an online autotuner that matches incoming inference request shapes and hardware fingerprints to a small set of 'opset' candidates (operator/kernel bundles) and picks the one minimizing expected latency under SLO while bounding cost. This differs from prior kernel-sampler work by treating selections as opset-level routing decisions, incorporating attention-mode heuristics (e.g., block-sparse / flash-attn availability), and explicitly co-optimizing prefill vs decode scheduling for mixed workloads.
background: We regularly see suboptimal choices when the runtime picks kernels independently for prefill and decode phases under mixed seq-len traffic on heterogeneous GPU fleets. Current heuristics either rely on heavy offline profiling or simplistic seqlen thresholds. Customers report tail latency spikes for bursty short-decoding requests that hop between model variants. The opset matcher idea groups compatible kernel implementations (memory layout, attention mode, quantization path) and scores them with a light-weight online estimator.
benchmarks: microbench: prefill(1024)->decode(64) across a40 vs h100 (2025-02-08)
acceptance_criteria: 1) New autotuner reduces 95th percentile end-to-end latency by >= 15% for mixed short-decode workloads vs baseline heuristic
2) No regression on 99th decode-only tail latency (> -2% relative) across supported GPU types
3) Cost-per-token delta within +/-5% compared to baseline or accompanied by documented trade-off
4) Falls back deterministically to safe opset when opset candidates are incompatible with pinned model version
5) Unit and integration tests covering opset compatibility matrix and decision telemetry are present
implementation_notes: Phase 1: offline fingerprint sweep to generate opset candidates from existing kernel catalog (arch x seqlen x batch)
Phase 2: lightweight online estimator (exponential moving averages of per-op latency with context keys: gpu_arch, batch, prefill_len, decode_len)
Phase 3: decision policy: score = latency_est + lambda * cost_est + penalty(prefill-decode-switch) where lambda is tunable per-customer
Use Bayesian bootstrap when sparse data; seed estimator from offline sweep to avoid long cold-starts
Capture feature toggles to disable attention-mode switching (e.g., when flash-attn incompatibilities detected)
tradeoffs_and_risks: Risk: frequent opset switching can increase cache thrash and KV cache misses — mitigate with sticky-policy windowing
Tradeoff: larger opset groups reduce switching but may miss specialized microkernels for extreme seqlens
Operational risk: telemetry volume increases due to per-request decision traces; add sampling and aggregated histograms
Compatibility risk: some quantized paths cannot be mixed between prefill/decode; ensure canonical fallback opset
milestones: 2025-02-05: offline sweep tooling and seed corpus generated
2025-02-18: landed runtime estimator and decision hook (canary)
2025-03-05: rollout to 25% of dedicated fleet for A/B
canary_notes: Canary uses traffic tag 'ops-match-v1' and targets low-risk customers with no strict latency SLOs
Initial sticky-window set to 60s; observation: some 1-2s latency regressions on rare GPU/driver combos — investigating fallback logic

notes: This ticket intentionally keeps the decision boundary interpretable (score-based) rather than a monolithic ML model to simplify audits and per-customer tuning. Long-term follow-up may explore a learned policy but only after stable telemetry and guardrails are in place.
